subject: Quality monitoring: regression detection, prompt-set rollouts and canary/rollback plan
messages:

Subject: Re: Quality monitoring kickoff and next steps

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward with a staged rollout of the assistant across two product flows (triage bot and intake summarizer). Before we start, our security and ops teams want a concrete plan for:

- how you will catch regressions tied to promptset changes,
- what the canary window looks like (metrics & duration), and
- automated rollback triggers we can trust in production.

Can Marissa or your eng team share a recommended: prompt-set versioning + eval harness integration + alerting matrix? Ideally this is a checklist we can run during our onboarding sprints.

Thanks,
Samir
Bluewell Health — Product Ops

[attachment: initial_requirements.pdf]

Hi Samir — looping Marissa (CS lead) and Karthik (in infra/edge on QMon) on this thread. Putting a short proposal below and we can iterate.

Quick proposal (high level):
1) Prompt-set/versioning: we recommend shipping prompt sets as CSVs with example prompts, expected outputs, and severity labels. Use semver style versioning (v1.0.0 -> v1.1.0 for minor tuning).
2) Eval harness: each prompt set is wired into the eval harness (pytest-like runner) so PRs to prompt sets run regression checks and produce a pass/fail and metric diffs (BLEU / accept rate / custom QA metrics).
3) Canary policy: 48-hour canary with daily evaluation buckets; primary metric is P0 (incorrect-critical) rate and secondary is latency & degradations in entity-extraction F1.
4) Rollback: automated rollback if P0 increases by >50% relative to baseline AND absolute P0 > 0.5% for two consecutive runs OR if latency SLO breaks by >25%.

Marissa — do you want to drop the CS implementation checklist and a timeline? Karthik — can you sketch the integration steps (eval harness -> prod monitoring -> alert hooks) and the minimal telemetry we need from Bluewell to enable the thresholds?

Best,
Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Samir — thanks, Ben. I attached a CS onboarding checklist and the initial prompt-set CSV (qmon_promptset_v1.csv) with test cases mapped to severity. High level implementation plan (CS + Implementation team):

- Week 0: Confirm production flows + map critical prompts (we've done this in the discovery doc).
- Week 1: Deliver prompt-set v1 (attached) and wire to eval harness. Raw outputs to be stored in the shared Drive (link below).
- Week 2: Run internal regression sweep against staging baseline (v0.9).
- Week 3: Canary rollout (10% traffic) with 48-hour monitoring window. Daily reports delivered to Bluewell Slack channel.
- Week 4: If stable, 100% promotion and runway monitoring for 7 days.

Acceptance and alert rules we propose (we can make these configurable):
- Blocker (P0): any hallucination on PHI extraction or incorrect discharge instructions — immediate rollback trigger.
- High (P1): semantic mismatches >10% — page on second consecutive daily failure.
- Perf: avg token latency > 400ms or 95th pct exceeds 850ms — alert.

Attachments: qmon_promptset_v1.csv, eval_integration_notes.md

Samir — can your ops team give us a sample of the production traffic profile for the triage flow (qps & average seq len)? That will let Karthik size the canary buckets.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole

Adding technical details to Marissa's plan. Summary of integration steps and automated triggers we will implement from the Redwood side:

1) Eval harness integration
   - Prompt set CSV -> eval runner (containerized) -> produces metrics JSON and diffs against baseline.
   - Each eval run creates an 'eval artefact' stored in S3 and a pointer in the run database.
   - PRs to prompt sets run these checks as part of CI; failures block merges.

2) Monitoring pipeline
   - Instrument token-level traces and prediction labels. Telemetry we need from Bluewell: example inputs (anonymized), expected label mapping for critical prompts, and traffic sample.
   - Metrics aggregated in per-hour buckets; evaluation job computes P0/P1 rates and compares to baseline (rolling 7-day median).

3) Canary orchestration
   - Canary window: configurable; default 48h. Canary sizes: 10% then 25% (if stable).
   - Daily automated eval run against a holdout prompt set and traffic sample; results posted to shared Drive and to Bluewell Slack channel.

4) Automated rollback logic (will be implemented as a policy in the deployment controller):
   - Trigger when BOTH:
     a) P0 delta > 50% relative to baseline AND absolute P0 > 0.5% for two consecutive evals, OR
     b) latency SLO violation: 95th percentile latency > SLO * 1.25 for two consecutive windows.
   - Rollback action: immediate route change to previous stable model variant + alert paging to oncall + create rollback ticket INF-7123.

5) Manual override and dry-run
   - All automated triggers will have a 30-min suppression window during which a human can confirm/abort. We will also provide a dry-run mode that simulates rollbacks without changing routing.

Next steps from infra: please share traffic sample (anonymized) and we will produce an initial baseline within 48 hours of receipt.

- Karthik
